Well, let me think about this year. My 3 mu is not much land, so I have to be careful with every yuan. But I also cannot afford a bad harvest — 3 mu is already small, if yield drops I lose a lot.

I split my land like this: 1 mu for cotton by itself (cotton takes the whole season April to October, cannot double-crop with it), and 2 mu for the wheat-maize rotation like most neighbors do here in Quzhou.

**Wheat (2 mu, winter):** I plant Jimai or Shixin variety — improved seeds, my neighbor got good results last year. I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before sowing, about 50 jin per mu as base, then top-dress with urea at jointing. That comes to roughly 20 kg N, 8 kg P, 7 kg K per mu. I irrigate 3 times — before winter, at jointing, and grain-filling. I have the well so water is not a problem, just the electricity cost. Two sprayings for aphids and yellow rust. I expect around 500 kg/mu if the weather cooperates — that is what I got last two years.

**Maize (2 mu, summer):** After wheat harvest I plant Zhengdan or similar hybrid right away, no-till, just sow into the stubble. Maize responds well to nitrogen — I put about 22 kg N per mu, mostly urea side-dressed at big-bell stage, plus about 6 kg P and 6 kg K from compound fertilizer at planting. One irrigation at tasseling usually enough with summer rain. Spray twice — once for corn borer, once for aphids. Target 550 kg/mu.

**Cotton (1 mu):** Cotton is more work and more risk, but price is okay. I use improved Bt cotton seed — saves on bollworm spraying but still need to spray for aphids, spider mites, plant bugs. I apply about 18 kg N per mu (split between base and flowering), 7 kg P, 9 kg K — cotton needs potassium for the bolls. Irrigate 3 times. I still have to spray 6-7 times total because cotton has many pests besides bollworm. Target 270 kg seed cotton per mu.

Plough for wheat after maize — deeper tillage helps roots. Rotary for maize into wheat stubble. For cotton I plough in spring.
